sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No.3046 of 2020, which is an application for exemption from filing certified copy.

2. Record of below Tribunal has already been received, therefore, IA is allowed and appellant is exempted from filing the certified copy.
3.
With the consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally.

4. Appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (in short 'MV' Act)
being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 25.03.2020 passed by the II MACT, Jaora, District Ratlam in MACT Case No.40/2016 setting aside the impugned award.

5. Brief facts of the case are that on 08.09.2014 when the deceased Shivram, injured Ajay and Aman went to Chambal river for immersion of Ganesh ji, while returning from Chambal river they were travelling in tractor and trolley bearing Registration No.MP-43-AB-1513, at that time, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor, suddenly trolley turned and turtle, due to which Shivram succumbed to death and Ajay and Aman sustained grievous injuries.

6. Claimant Ajay / respondent No.1 has preferred claim petition before the II Additional Member,
MACT, Jaora, District Ratlam of compensation of Rs.3,55,000/- for injured Ajay.
The below Tribunal after framing the issues and recording evidence of both the parties has awarded compensation of Rs.60,000/- in favour of respondent No.1.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, the claim petition has filed.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that respondent Nos.3 and 4 are the owners of the offending tractor / trolley, but the trolley was not insured with appellant / Insurance Company on the date of accident, but the trial Court was not insured, therefore, Insurance Company has not taken any premium to recover risk of trolley and passengers travelling in trolley.
Tractor was not used for agricultural purpose at the time of incident and condition of insurance policy has been violated.
Hence, he prays that impugned award be set aside.

8. Per contra, counsel for the respondents oppose the prayer by submitting that impugned order passed by the below tribunal is just and proper and does not deserve for any interference,
9.

It is an admitted position that at the time of incident, concerned aforesaid trolley was not insured with the appellant / Insurance Company, but trial Court was not insured by the appellant and appellant / Insurance Company has not taken any premium to recover risk of trolley and passengers travelling in the said trolley.
10.
Learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance upon the judgment of Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of Dhondubai Vs . Hanmantappa Bandappa Gandigude since deceased Thru.

his LRs &
Ors. 2023 Live Law (SC) 725 in which Hon'ble the Apex Court held that "in a matter of the present nature, the law is well settled that when a tractor and trailer are involved, both the tractor as well as the trailer are required to be insured.

Therefore, in a normal circumstance, when the appellant /
claimant was travelling in the trailer which was not insured,

11. This citation is fully applicable in the present appeal.

12. On the basis of aforesaid law laid down by Hon'ble the Apex Court this appeal is partly allowed and it is directed that the appellant shall pay the amount awarded to the below Tribunal as compensation with the actual interest and shall recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
The amount shall be deposited before the MACT within six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order, thereafter, the same shall be disbursed to the concerned.
13. The appeal is disposed off accordingly,
14. All other pending interim applications are also stands disposed off.
